In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no aetiological association between diabetes mellitus on the one hand and optic atrophy or nerve deafness on the other.
diabetes mellitus and primary optic atrophy are fortuitously associated, and that the association of diabetes with nerve deafness is also probably fortuitous.
there is an association between diabetes mellitus, optic atrophy, and nerve deafness in certain families but that this association does not constitute an aetiological sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diabetes, optic atrophy, and nerve deafness are all present in the same generation, but that the association of the first two is not necessarily associated with the last.

in a family of 13 members there are two cases of diabetes mellitus, one of bilateral optic atrophy and one of bilateral nerve deafness, all in one generation; in addition, there is one case of diabetes mellitus in the preceding generation, one of bilateral deafness in the next generation, and one of bilateral deaf ness in the generation after that.

in the family of the mother, father, and four daughters, diabetes mellitus and nerve deafness occurred in the mother and in two daughters, while optic atrophy was present in the mother and one daughter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important for patients to be screened for hearing loss and for physicians to be aware of the association between diabetes and hearing loss.

the association of optic atrophy and bilateral nerve deafness with diabetes is a rare occurrence, and that in the presence of these findings the possibility of an inherited metabolic defect should be borne in mind.
the association of optic atrophy and deafness in the presence of diabetes mellitus is a strong indicator for the presence of a mitochondrial disease.
